title: Longitudinal MRI learning classifies treated high-grade glioma changes
summary: A support-vector machine combined structural and perfusion MRI measurements to classify progression, pseudoprogression and stable disease after high-grade glioma treatment. In a retrospective 64-patient study, longitudinal combined features reached reported accuracy of 94.7% in the 19-patient subset with serial perfusion scans. Repeated internal cross-validation, a mostly clinical imaging reference and feature-selection uncertainty limit generalization; no prospective treatment benefit was demonstrated.
ai_technology: Radial-basis-function support-vector machine; LASSO feature selection
organization: University College London; University College London Hospitals; The Netherlands Cancer Institute

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Repeated internal two-fold cross-validation with histology in 13 patients and longitudinal clinical/radiological consensus in the others; serial perfusion available in 19 patients.
evidence.unknown: External frozen-model performance and clinical benefit remain unestablished; the small serial-scan subset, reference incorporation and feature-selection timing can inflate apparent accuracy.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO selects image-derived measurements and an RBF support-vector classifier combines structural/perfusion changes to distinguish recorded post-treatment categories.
